subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the equation of the plane passing through the point (3, −2, −1) and perpendicular to the vector (4, 7, −4).

mark_split.label: Write the point and the normal as vectors

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.73, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 30. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 split rewards writing the point and the normal as vectors, stating the perpendicularity condition, expanding it in coordinates, and simplifying to the finished equation. PRINTED DEFECT RECORDED: the book prints the point as (3, −2, −1) in the stem, but its own working carries a third component of +1, that is (3, −2, 1). This card is authored from the stem as printed, (3, −2, −1), which gives 4x + 7y − 4z − 2 = 0; the book's working point would give 4x + 7y − 4z + 6 = 0. Nothing was silently repaired and nothing was skipped. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints 8 short answers at 4 marks each and the student answers any 6; Product of Vectors is one of the units that can fill a Section-B slot. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the equation of a plane through a given point with a given normal vector.

steps.label: Write the vectors
steps.margin_note: First mark. The vector (4, 7, −4) is given as a triple, so write it in i, j, k form before using it. r is the position vector of a general point of the plane.
steps.memory_tip: A triple in brackets is a vector. Write it in i, j, k form before using it.
lines: Let A be the point (3, −2, −1), so
Let P(x, y, z) be any point of the plane,

recall.must_convey: That the point and the normal are written as vectors a = 3i − 2j − k and n = 4i + 7j − 4k, with r a general point.
accept: write the point as three i minus two j minus k and the normal as four i plus seven j minus four k
turn the two triples into i j k vectors
let r be the position vector of any point of the plane
point ni vector ga rasta, normal ni kuda
a is three i minus two j minus k and n is four i plus seven j minus four k
reject: the condition is r minus a dot n is zero

steps.why: The plane equation is built from a dot product, and a dot product needs vectors, not coordinate triples.
common_mistakes: Reading (4, 7, −4) as a point instead of the normal vector.
Missing the minus sign on the third coordinate of the point.

steps.label: State the condition
steps.margin_note: Second mark. AP is drawn inside the plane, and n is at right angles to the plane, so their dot product is zero. That one equation IS the plane.
steps.memory_tip: Every line drawn inside the plane is at right angles to the normal, so the dot product is zero.
lines: AP lies in the plane and n is at right
angles to the plane, so AP ⊥ n.

recall.must_convey: That r − a lies in the plane and is therefore at right angles to n, giving (r − a)·n = 0.
accept: r minus a lies in the plane so its dot product with the normal is zero
the condition is r minus a dot n equals zero
AP is perpendicular to the normal
r minus a dot n zero avthundi
any line inside the plane is at right angles to the normal
reject: write the point and the normal

steps.why: A plane is exactly the set of points P for which AP is at right angles to the normal. Writing that as a dot product turns the geometry into one equation.
common_mistakes: Writing r·n = 0, which is the plane through the origin instead.
Taking a cross product, which gives a vector and not an equation.

steps.label: Expand in coordinates
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Subtract the point coordinate by coordinate. x − 3, then y − (−2) = y + 2, then z − (−1) = z + 1.
steps.memory_tip: Subtracting a negative coordinate adds. y + 2 and z + 1, not y − 2 and z − 1.

recall.must_convey: That r − a is (x − 3)i + (y + 2)j + (z + 1)k and the dot product with n gives 4(x − 3) + 7(y + 2) − 4(z + 1) = 0.
accept: r minus a is x minus three, y plus two, z plus one
four times x minus three plus seven times y plus two minus four times z plus one equals zero
expand the dot product coordinate by coordinate
y plus two and z plus one, minus sign valla plus avthundi
write out the dot product in x y z

steps.why: Subtracting a negative coordinate adds, so two of the three brackets carry a plus. That is where most of the marks are lost on this question.
common_mistakes: Writing y − 2 and z − 1 instead of y + 2 and z + 1.
Multiplying the brackets by the coordinates of the point instead of the normal.

steps.label: Simplify
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The three constants are −12, +14 and −4, which add to −2. Put the point back in as a one-line check.
steps.memory_tip: The constants are −12, +14 and −4, and they add to −2.

recall.must_convey: That the equation simplifies to 4x + 7y − 4z − 2 = 0, and that the given point satisfies it.
accept: the plane is four x plus seven y minus four z minus two equals zero
the constants add to minus two
putting the point back gives zero so the answer is right
final answer four x plus seven y minus four z equals two
collect the constants and write the equation

steps.why: Collecting the constants is the only arithmetic in the question, so the substitution check at the end is worth the one extra line.
common_mistakes: Adding the three constants to −22 or +2 by a sign slip.
Leaving the answer with the brackets unexpanded.
